subject: Transforming a vector to a matrix in the transformed parameters block

messages.author: fde4048c840328bf
messages.subject: Transforming a vector to a matrix in the transformed parameters block
parts:
Hi all!

So, this is something I would like to do. I want to estimate a lower triangular matrix with ones in the main diagonal. I will need the matrix in the transformed parameters block. The idea is that I define a column vector of parameters that contains the off-lower-diagonal elements of the matrix, and then, in the transformed parameters block, I define,

matrix[M,M]             A;
int                     indexA;

// Build matrix A
A          <- diag_matrix(rep_vector(1, M));
indexA     <- 1;


    for(k in 2:M){
        for (m in 1:(k-1)){
            A[k,m]     <- A1[(indexA+m-1)];
        }
       
        indexA      <- indexA + k - 1;
    }


where A1 is the vector of parameters that I am estimating. However, it is true that the transformed parameters block does not accept integers, and I have defined an auxiliar integer "indexA" to construct the matrix. Obviously, I get an error from STAB... Is there anyway to do this, without constructing the matrix manually cell by cell? (Let's say that M is quite big...)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Transforming a vector to a matrix in the transformed parameters block
parts:
You can declare indexA as a local variable. Just one more
set of brackets:

transformed parameters {

matrix[M,M] A; // transformed parameter
{
int indexA; // local variable
A <- ...
...
}

Then indexA is a local variable and you can use it however you
like.

- Bob
